items.descriptionOriginal: Οι πτήσεις στις Ηνωμένες Πολιτείες εκτελούνται ξανά, όμως η επανεκκίνηση των πτήσεων δεν σημαίνει και άμεση επιστροφή στην κανονικότητα. Οι εταιρείες προσπαθούν να επαναφέρουν αεροσκάφη και πληρώματα στις βάσεις τους, ώστε να εκτελέσουν ξανά τα δρομολόγια. Μιλώντας στο NBC, ο υπουργός Μεταφορών, Σον Ντάφι, δήλωσε ότι οι διαταραχές στις αεροπορικές μεταφορές θα έχουν τελειώσει στο «τέλος της σημερινής ή της αυριανής μέρας». «Θα δούμε την κατάσταση να επιστρέφει στο φυσιολογικό σήμερα και στην πλήρη κανονικότητα αύριο», πρόσθεσε. Ανταπόκριση από Νέα Υόρκη: Γεωργία Γαραντζιώτη Το πρόβλημα είναι αλυσιδωτό. Αεροσκάφη και πληρώματα βρίσκονται σε διαφορετικά αεροδρόμια από εκείνα όπου χρειάζονται, ενώ πολλοί πιλότοι και αεροσυνοδοί συμπλήρωσαν το ανώτατο επιτρεπόμενο ωράριο εργασίας. Και όλα φαίνεται πως ξεκίνησαν από ένα ρούτερ στο Αρκάνσας . Σύμφωνα με αποκάλυψη τη Wall Street Journal , λίγο μετά την εγκατάστασή της, η συσκευή άρχισε να στέλνει τεράστιο όγκο δεδομένων, υπερφορτώνοντας το παλιό τηλεπικοινωνιακό δίκτυο της Ομοσπονδιακής Υπηρεσίας Πολιτικής Αεροπορίας των ΗΠΑ. Η εφημερίδα δημοσιεύει ηχογραφημένες συνομιλίες που αποτυπώνουν την κλιμάκωση της κρίσης: παράσιτα στις συχνότητες, πιλότοι που δεν άκουγαν τους ελεγκτές και τελικά την εντολή να σταματήσουν οι απογειώσεις σε ολόκληρη τη χώρα. Προβλήματα επικοινωνίας καταγράφηκαν σύμφωνα με αμερικανικά μέσα στα 17 από τα 22 κέντρα ελέγχου πτήσεων μεγάλου ύψους. Τώρα ερευνάται αν έφταιξε ο εξοπλισμός ή η εγκατάστασή του, αν ήταν δηλαδή ανθρώπινο λάθος. Οι αρχές εκτιμούν ότι τα δρομολόγια θα ομαλοποιηθούν εντελώς έως απόψε το βράδυ, όμως για τους επιβάτες η αναμονή και η ταλαιπωρία συνεχίζεται. Πηγή: Reuters Διαβάστε επίσης: ΗΠΑ: Το απαρχαιωμένο σύστημα ελέγχου εναέριας κυκλοφορίας πίσω από το αεροπορικό χάος – Χιλιάδες νέες ακυρώσεις πτήσεων www.ertnews.gr

items.descriptionOriginal: Τις τελευταίες εξελίξεις γύρω από την ηλεκτρική διασύνδεση Ελλάδας – Κύπρου περιέγραψε ο Άγγελος Συρίγος , βουλευτής της Νέας Δημοκρατίας και καθηγητής Διεθνούς Δικαίου και Εξωτερικής Πολιτικής του Παντείου Πανεπιστημίου, μιλώντας στην εκπομπή Update του ΕΡΤnews. Ο κ. Συρίγος τόνισε ότι « το γαλλικό πλοίο θα ολοκληρώσει τις έρευνές του μέχρι τα τέλη Μαρτίου και έπειτα περνάμε σε μια νέα φάση, όπου θα ξεκινήσουν οι εργασίες για να τοποθετηθεί το καλώδιο και ενδεχομένως να σημειωθεί μια δεύτερη φάση εντάσεως με την τουρκική πλευρά». Την ίδια ώρα, σχολίασε τη γαλλική ρηματική διακοίνωση, σχολιάζοντας ότι «οι Γάλλοι λένε ότι προβαίνουν σε γνωστοποίηση προς τις τουρκικές αρχές χωρίς να έχουν νομική υποχρέωση», ενώ πρόσθεσε ότι « δεν αναφέρεται καθόλου η σύμφωνη γνώμη των ελληνικών αρχών ». Δείτε περισσότερα στο ertflix.gr | Ακούστε περισσότερα στο ertecho.gr «Αίτηση για άδεια υποβλήθηκε μόνο προς την ελληνική πλευρά» Όπως εξήγησε, « αυτό σημαίνει ότι στην Ελλάδα δεν δημιουργεί νομικό προηγούμενο » και επανέλαβε ότι «αίτηση για άδεια έχει υποβληθεί μόνο προς την ελληνική πλευρά». Ο κ. Συρίγος ανέφερε χαρακτηριστικά ότι δεν είναι ευτυχής από τη ρηματική διακοίνωση, ωστόσο διαβάζοντας το περιεχόμενό της, αντιλαμβάνεται ότι δεν δημιουργεί νομικό επιχείρημα υπέρ της Τουρκίας , διότι «αναφέρεται ότι δεν γίνεται στο πλαίσιο νομικής υποχρέωσης, αλλά στο πλαίσιο ανδροφροσύνης. Επίσης, δεν γίνεται εξουσιοδότηση της Ελλάδας. Αυτό σημαίνει ότι εμείς συνεχίζουμε να ακολουθούμε τη στάση που ακολουθούσαμε έως τώρα». Παράλληλα, επισήμανε ότι «στην Κάσο το 2024 υπήρξε μια τακτική υποχώρηση της Ελλάδας. Ωστόσο, τώρα αν υποχώρησε κάποιος κάποιος, είναι σαφές ότι υποχώρησαν οι Τούρκοι, οι οποίοι δέχθηκαν μια ασαφή και γενικόλογη γνωστοποίηση και αποδέχθηκαν τις έρευνες του πλοίου . «Καμία σχέση με την πραγματικότητα οι δηλώσεις Κιλιτσντάρογλου» Σχετικά με τις δηλώσεις του προέδρου του Ρεπουμπλικανικού Λαϊκού Κόμματος (CHP) της Τουρκίας, Κεμάλ Κιλιτσντάρογλου, για το ενδεχόμενο πολεμικής σύγκρουσης μεταξύ Τουρκίας και Ελλάδας, με αφορμή τη στρατιωτικοποίηση των νησιών, σχολίασε ότι «αυτές οι δηλώσεις δεν έχουν καμία σχέση με την πραγματικότητα» . « Η Ελλάδα έχει στρατεύματα στα νησιά από το 1974 και μετά και φυσικά δεν πρόκειται να αποσυρθούν . Είναι δικαίωμα της χώρας να έχει στρατεύματα σε όποιο σημείο στην επικράτεια επιθυμεί», ανέφερε χαρακτηριστικά. www.ertnews.gr

items.descriptionOriginal: Α πό τα βιολογικά ρολόγια και τις προσωπικές συνήθειες μέχρι τα γούρια, τις μικρές τελετουργίες και τις ιδιορρυθμίες των κορυφαίων αθλητών του πλανήτη. Ο Ράφα Ναδάλ, ο Μάικλ Φελπς και ένας Μίλτος που δεν χρειάζεται να ξυπνάει από τα χαράματα για να πετάξει πάνω από τα οκτώ μέτραau «Αυτός είναι πρωινός τύπος». Ο στάνταρ προσδιορισμός για κάποιους ανθρώπους που ανοίγουν τα μάτια τους στις 6:00 το πρωί, χαμογελούν στον ήλιο, φτιάχνουν καφέ, τρέχουν πέντε χιλιόμετρα και μέχρι τις 8:00 έχουν… προλάβει να επιλύσουν τα προβλήματα του πλανήτη. Είναι βέβαια κι εκείνοι που θεωρούν ότι το ξυπνητήρι μοιάζει με προσωπική προσβολή –και ψάχνουν με «τσίμπλα» στο μάτι ένα σφυρί για να το… εξολοθρεύσουν–, ότι ο καφές δεν είναι πολυτέλεια αλλά ανθρώπινο δικαίωμα και ότι πριν από τις 10:00 δεν πρέπει να τους ζητάς τίποτα περισσότερο από μια στοιχειώδη επικοινωνία. Ενδεχομένως, στη δεύτερη παράγραφο να έχουμε κιόλας το «οργανικό στίγμα» του Μίλτου Τεντόγλου. Ο Έλληνας Ολυμπιονίκης, παγκόσμιος πρωταθλητής και υπεραθλητής έχει εξηγήσει αρκετές φορές ότι δεν του αρέσει να αγωνίζεται νωρίς το πρωί. Δεν είναι απλώς μια ιδιοτροπία ή μια ατάκα που προκαλεί χαμόγελα. Έχει περιγράψει, με τον χαρακτηριστικό και αφοπλιστικό τρόπο του, ότι το σώμα του λειτουργεί διαφορετικά τις πρωινές ώρες, ότι δεν είναι άνθρωπος που ξυπνάει νωρίς και ότι ένας πρωινός αγώνας μπορεί να τον βγάλει από τον συνηθισμένο αγωνιστικό του ρυθμό. Έχει πει σε συνέντευξή του ότι το σώμα του παθαίνει σοκ! Κάπως έτσι, η πρόσφατη ανακοίνωση του προγράμματος για το Παγκόσμιο Πρωτάθλημα στίβου του 2027 στο Πεκίνο μοιάζει με ένα μικρό δώρο προς τον ίδιο. Εφόσον, φυσικά, εξασφαλίσει τη συμμετοχή του, ο προκριματικός του μήκους στις 14 Σεπτεμβρίου θα γίνει στις 19:15 τοπική ώρα, ενώ ο τελικός, στις 15 Σεπτεμβρίου, είναι προγραμματισμένος για βραδάκι, στις 20:51. Με άλλα λόγια κανείς δεν θα χρειαστεί και να τον βγάλει από το κρεβάτι για να διεκδικήσει μια θέση στον τελικό ή ένα ακόμη μετάλλιο… Το βιολογικό ρολόι δεν ρυθμίζεται από το πρόγραμμα των αγώνων Κάπου εδώ αρχίζει η πραγματικά ενδιαφέρουσα ιστορία. Γιατί το πότε αποδίδει καλύτερα ένας αθλητής, το πώς προετοιμάζεται ψυχολογικά και τι χρειάζεται για να αισθανθεί ότι έχει τον έλεγχο δεν είναι καθόλου αμελητέες λεπτομέρειες. Στον αθλητισμό υψηλού επιπέδου, η ψυχολογία δεν είναι διακοσμητικό στοιχείο. Είναι μέρος της καθημερινής δουλειάς. Οι αθλητές καλούνται να διαχειριστούν την πίεση, τις προσδοκίες, τον φόβο της αποτυχίας και την αβεβαιότητα ενός αποτελέσματος που συχνά κρίνεται σε ελάχιστα εκατοστά ή κλάσματα του δευτερολέπτου. Η χρονοβιολογία, η επιστήμη που μελετά τους βιολογικούς ρυθμούς, έχει μπει για τα καλά στη συζήτηση γύρω από την αθλητική απόδοση. Και όχι άδικα. Το σώμα δεν βρίσκεται στην ίδια κατάσταση στις επτά το πρωί και στις επτά το απόγευμα. Η θερμοκρασία του σώματος, η εγρήγορση, η νευρομυϊκή λειτουργία και η αίσθηση της κόπωσης μεταβάλλονται στη διάρκεια της ημέρας. Οι επιστήμονες επισημαίνουν ότι αρκετές παράμετροι της φυσικής απόδοσης, όπως η ταχύτητα, η ευκινησία και η δύναμη του άλματος, εμφανίζουν συχνά ευνοϊκότερες τιμές αργότερα μέσα στην ημέρα. Παράλληλα, υπογραμμίζουν τη σημασία του ατομικού, του προσωπικού δηλαδή βιολογικού ρολογιού που κάνει κάποιους ανθρώπους να λειτουργούν καλύτερα το πρωί και άλλους το απόγευμα ή το βράδυ. Στο Πεκίνο, τον Σεπτέμβριο του 2027, ο Μίλτος Τεντόγλου θα έχει, με το καλό, την ευκαιρία να αγωνιστεί σε ώρες που ταιριάζουν περισσότερο στον δικό του ρυθμό, εφόσον βρεθεί εκεί. Δεν πρόκειται να του χαρίσει κανείς ούτε εκατοστό στον διάδρομο. Ούτε να του εξασφαλίσει ένα μετάλλιο επειδή ο προκριματικός είναι βραδινός. Οι αντίπαλοι θα είναι εκεί, το άγχος θα είναι εκεί, η πίεση θα είναι εκεί. Αλλά τουλάχιστον δεν θα χρειαστεί να παλέψει και με το ξυπνητήρι. Κι αυτό, για έναν άνθρωπο που έχει δηλώσει δημοσίως ότι δεν είναι πρωινός τύπος, δεν είναι καθόλου μικρή υπόθεση. Διαβάστε ακόμα Κάθε πρωταθλητής στην ώρα και με την ώρα του Άλλωστε, ο αθλητισμός έχει χώρο για όλους τους βιορυθμούς. Και στον αθλητισμό υψηλού επιπέδου υπάρχει χώρος ακόμη και για… γούρια και προσωπικές τελετουργίες! Μια συγκεκριμένη κάλτσα, ένα αντικείμενο που ταξιδεύει μαζί με τον αθλητή, μια σταθερή σειρά κινήσεων, ένα τραγούδι, μια συγκεκριμένη διαδρομή μέχρι τον αγωνιστικό χώρο. Η επιστήμη δεν υποστηρίζει ότι ένα γούρι μπορεί να αλλάξει το αποτέλεσμα ενός αγώνα. Μπορεί, όμως, μια γνώριμη συνήθεια να προσφέρει αίσθηση σταθερότητας, να περιορίσει τους περισπασμούς και να βοηθήσει τον αθλητή να διαχειριστεί το άγχος του. Η διαφορά ανάμεσα στην προληπτική συνήθεια και την ψυχολογική προετοιμασία είναι λεπτή, αλλά ουσιαστική. Ο Ναδάλ και οι μπουκάλες, ο Φελπς και το soundtrack Αν υπάρχει ένας άνθρωπος που έκανε τις μικρές αγωνιστικές συνήθειες παγκόσμιο τηλεοπτικό θέαμα, αυτός είναι ο Ράφα Ναδάλ. Δύο μπουκάλια νερού, τοποθετημένα με συγκεκριμένη σειρά και με τις ετικέτες στραμμένες προς την ίδια κατεύθυνση. Μικρές, επαναλαμβανόμενες κινήσεις πριν από το σερβίς. Το άγγιγμα των μαλλιών, η τακτοποίηση της μπλούζας, η προσεκτική προετοιμασία πριν από κάθε πόντο. Και, φυσικά, η σχεδόν θρησκευτική αποφυγή των γραμμών του γηπέδου όταν περπατά. Για κάποιον που παρακολουθεί απλώς έναν αγώνα τένις, όλα αυτά μπορεί να μοιάζουν με μια περίεργη συλλογή από προλήψεις. Για τον ίδιο τον Ισπανό, όμως, είχαν διαφορετική εξήγηση. Η επανάληψη των ίδιων κινήσεων τον βοηθούσε να συγκεντρώνεται, να περιορίζει τους περισπασμούς και να αισθάνεται ότι βάζει μια τάξη στο περιβάλλον του. Ο Μάικλ Φελπς είχε άλλη προσέγγιση. Πριν από τους αγώνες, τα ακουστικά ήταν σχεδόν προέκταση του σώματός του. Hip-hop, rap και μουσική που τον βοηθούσε να απομονώσει τον εξωτερικό θόρυβο, να βρει τον ρυθμό του και να συγκεντρωθεί σε αυτό που ερχόταν. Ο ίδιος είχε εξηγήσει ότι άκουγε μουσική μέχρι την τελευταία δυνατή στιγμή πριν από την εκκίνηση. Δεν ήταν απλώς μια μουσική προτίμηση. Ήταν ένα προσωπικό καταφύγιο, ένας τρόπος να κλείσει την πόρτα στις προσδοκίες, στους αντιπάλους και στον θόρυβο μιας διοργάνωσης που απαιτούσε από εκείνον να είναι σχεδόν υπεράνθρωπος. Ο Τεντόγλου δεν χρειάζεται να υποδυθεί τον πρωταθλητή Ο Μίλτος, θεωρώ, έχει ένα επιπλέον πλεονέκτημα σε σχέση με αυτά και άλλα «ιερά τέρατα» του παγκόσμιου αθλητισμού: δεν προσπαθεί να κατασκευάσει μια εικόνα πρωταθλητή με βάση τα κλισέ που συνοδεύουν συνήθως τους μεγάλους αθλητές. Έχει μιλήσει ανοιχτά για την αγάπη του για τα videogames, την τεχνολογία, το design, την ιαπωνική κουλτούρα και τα anime. Έχει παραδεχθεί ότι βαριέται την προπόνηση, ότι αγαπάει να αράζει στο σπίτι και ότι δεν θέλει να γεμίζει την καθημερινότητά του με ατελείωτες υποχρεώσεις. Με λίγα λόγια, δεν αισθάνεται την ανάγκη να υποδύεται τον αθλητή 24 ώρες το εικοσιτετράωρο. Και αυτό είναι μέρος της γοητείας του. Η προσωπικότητα ενός αθλητή δεν εξαφανίζεται όταν φοράει τη φόρμα της εθνικής ομάδας. Αντίθετα, κουβαλάει μαζί της τις συνήθειες, τις αναφορές και τις μικρές απολαύσεις που τον κάνουν αυτό που είναι. Ο Τεντόγλου έχει επίσης εκφραστεί με θαυμασμό για τον Κουβανό Ιβάν Πεδρόσο, τον οποίο θεωρεί σημείο αναφοράς, ενώ έχει παραδεχθεί ότι παρατηρεί και υιοθετεί τεχνικά στοιχεία από κορυφαίους αθλητές του τριπλούν, όπως ο Πιτσάρδο και ο Κρίστιαν Τέιλορ. Μελετά, παρατηρεί, προσαρμόζει. Δεν είναι όλα έμπνευση της στιγμής. Είναι και η δουλειά που γίνεται πίσω από την εικόνα του χαλαρού τύπου που μοιάζει να μην παίρνει τίποτα πολύ στα σοβαρά. Ακόμη και μέσα στον αγώνα έχει τις δικές του ψυχολογικές μεθόδους. Έχει περιγράψει πώς μιλάει στον εαυτό του, πώς προσπαθεί να τον αφυπνίσει όταν δεν αποδίδει όπως θέλει και πώς χρησιμοποιεί ακόμη και μια προκλητική κίνηση για να ανεβάσει την αδρεναλίνη του. Σαν να δημιουργεί ο ίδιος την ένταση που χρειάζεται για να μπει στην κατάλληλη αγωνιστική κατάσταση. Δεν χρειάζεται να φοράει την πανοπλία του υπεραθλητή κάθε πρωί. Μπορεί να είναι ο Μίλτος που βαριέται, που παίζει videogames, που αγαπάει τα anime και που δεν θέλει να σηκώνεται νωρίς. Και το απόγευμα να γίνει ο Μίλτος που πετάει πάνω από τα οκτώ μέτρα. Γιατί ο Τεντόγλου έχει το δικό του «σύμπαν». Και δεν μοιάζει με κανενός άλλου! Η σκλήρυνση είναι το βήμα που σκληραίνει τα χρώματα, κόλλα…
items.descriptionOriginal: Nanyang Technological University (NTU) and automotive supplier Motherson are working to adapt a magnetic curing method called Spinheat for factory use, according to an NTU news release. NTU said one-hour magnetic curing produced adhesive joints with bonding strength comparable to a 24-hour oven cure. Curing is the step that hardens paints, adhesives and resins. Spinheat mixes magnetic nanoparticles into the material. When an alternating magnetic field, one that rapidly reverses direction, passes through, the particles heat the material from inside, so the whole component doesn’t need to sit in an oven, the release said. NTU’s research is led by professor Raju V. Ramanujan and associate professor Terry Steele, both in the School of Materials Science and Engineering. The latest version of Spinheat adjusts the magnetic field using real-time temperature feedback, the release said. Motherson will help test it under conditions closer to industrial production. Feedback control during curing NTU first showed epoxy curing with a magnetic field in 2020 with its magnetocuring glue , according to the release . The latest research appeared in Applied Materials Today. In a separate experiment, the authors mixed doped ferrite magnetic nanoparticles into a thermoset epoxy resin, a plastic that hardens permanently, and heated it with the field. A microprocessor adjusted the field strength as temperatures changed, the paper said. The release said the approach could also prevent heat damage to other parts of a component, particularly those made of heat-sensitive materials. Epoxy curing releases its own heat, and that heat can run away. The abstract said feedback-controlled heating prevented that runaway and reduced voids, or gas pockets, from 33.0 percent to 5.3 percent of the volume, as measured by nano-computed tomography, a 3D X-ray imaging method. The authors’ preprint, an earlier version posted online on SSRN, also said the samples reached their target temperatures within 180 seconds. Motherson, which the release said supports customers from mote than 475 facilities across 47 countries, brings automotive engineering and manufacturing capabilities to the collaboration. Limits and next steps The results come from laboratory samples. The published paper reported lap shear strength, a measure of how well a joint resists sliding forces, of 7.2 megapascals for the one-hour magnetic cure and 7.3 megapascals for the 24-hour oven cure, with uncertainties of 1.4 and 2.2 megapascals. Those ranges overlap, so the strengths are comparable, not proven identical. The release gives no measured energy savings, so its energy and emissions benefits are projections. Steele said the next challenge is to understand “how this can work reliably within automotive manufacturing.” The researchers are still seeking to test Spinheat closer to factory conditions, particularly for paints and coatings, and will study coating thickness, curing speed, temperature control and component sizes and shapes. Other groups are also targeting cure time, including Toray CMA, which says its fast-cure composite cuts curing by up to 45 percent. NTU is exploring commercialization, including start-up options, and filed intellectual property through NTUitive, its innovation company. The paper appeared in the April 2026 issue of Applied Materials Today.

items.descriptionOriginal: You wake up and your nose is the first thing to tell you what the air is like. One side is blocked, then the other. There is a dull pressure behind your cheeks, your eyes itch, and the sky outside is the colour of dishwater. You open the AQI app and it says "severe" . Then the questions begin. Is this my sinusitis flaring up? An allergy? Or is it just the smog? Should I reach for that decongestant spray in the drawer? Do I need a doctor, or will this pass when the air clears? If you live in Delhi NCR with chronic sinusitis or allergic rhinitis, you may know this morning well. Your nose was inflamed long before the first particle of smog arrived, and now you're left guessing, often with whatever is nearest to hand. Dr M. Shantanu, an ENT specialist in Delhi, says that guesswork is where people go wrong. "Not every blocked nose is sinusitis," he says, and treating it as if it were can backfire. Here are his answers to the questions people ask most on bad air days, as a field guide for when the sky turns grey. It does not replace a consultation with your own doctor. Why smog hits sinus and allergy patients harder Why does a high AQI make a blocked nose worse? "Think of the nose as a security checkpoint. Mucus and tiny hair-like structures called cilia catch dust, allergens, and microorganisms, while the sinuses rely on that same system to drain," he explains. People living with chronic sinusitis may experience increased congestion, facial pressure and reduced smell during periods of severe air pollution. Photograph: (TNIE) When fine particles slip in, they irritate the lining and set off inflammation. The swelling narrows the small passages linking the sinuses to the nose. Drainage slows, and an old problem feels brand new. Dr Shantanu points to research linking particulate exposure with chronic rhinosinusitis and with greater severity. If your congestion, sneezing, facial pressure, postnasal drip, headaches or dulled sense of smell keep flaring when the air is bad, he says, take it as a cue to identify your triggers. Which pollutants are the troublemakers? PM2.5 and PM10, particles measuring 2.5 and 10 micrometres or less, top his list. They arrive via vehicle exhaust, construction dust, industrial emissions and smoke. Traffic-related nitrogen dioxide, a gas produced mainly by burning fuel, adds to the irritation. "If you live or work near a building site, expect more sneezing and a runnier nose, especially if you have allergies," he says. Is it sinusitis, allergy, or just pollution irritation? The three overlap, so Dr Shantanu reads the pattern. Pollution irritation burns, blocks, and makes you sneeze during or after exposure, usually without fever. Allergic rhinitis brings sneezing, an itchy nose, watery eyes and a runny nose after contact with pollen, dust mites or pet dander. Sinusitis means congestion, facial pressure, reduced smell and nasal discharge, sometimes with fever. Chronic rhinosinusitis generally means symptoms lasting at least 12 weeks. Pollution and allergy can also feed each other, so your symptoms may refuse to sit in one box. Can a smoggy day give me a sinus infection? Not automatically, he says. " Pollution can make symptoms harder to control in people who already have a nasal or sinus condition." Allergic rhinitis can cause repeated sneezing, itchy eyes, nasal irritation and a runny nose when pollution levels rise. Photograph: ( TNIE ) Viral infections, especially colds, are the most common cause of acute sinus infections. Mucus colour alone cannot confirm a bacterial infection. Your cause, the duration of symptoms, and a clinical examination should decide treatment, because not every blocked nose needs antibiotics. What does it do to daily life? Persistent congestion, sleep broken by difficulty breathing through the nose, a foggy head, repeated flare-ups and allergies that are harder to manage. Dr Shantanu adds that not everyone who breathes dirty air develops chronic sinusitis . Genetics, allergies, nasal anatomy, infections, and smoking all shape individual risk. His survival guide for a high-AQI day Where do I start? Check the AQI before you plan anything outdoors. When it is poor, cut both the length and the intensity of outdoor exercise, especially near busy roads and construction sites. Saline nasal sprays and rinses can help clear mucus and trapped irritants, provided sterile, distilled or boiled-and-cooled water is used. Photograph: ( Dreamstime ) Keep a note of whether your symptoms worsen on high-pollution days. That record helps an ENT specialist pin down your triggers. Reduce smoke and chemical fumes at home too, and follow workplace safety measures if your job is dusty. Does a mask really help? A well-fitting N95 worn outdoors can cut inhalation of many airborne particles. It is not a force field, though. It does not remove every harmful gas, so he treats it as one layer of protection and not the whole answer. Ordinary cloth or surgical masks do far less against fine particles. How do I keep my home air cleaner? Keep windows and doors shut when the air outside is bad, and run a correctly sized HEPA purifier if you have one. HEPA air purifiers can help reduce indoor particulate pollution, while limiting incense, cigarette smoke and other indoor pollutants. Photograph: ( India Today ) Skip cigarettes, incense, and other indoor smoke. Open up the house only when the air outside is cleaner than the air inside. How do I rinse my nose safely? Saline sprays or rinses clear mucus and irritants, so they suit the end of a day spent outside. The water is what makes it safe: distilled, sterile, or boiled and cooled. Never untreated tap water. Clean the device as its instructions say. Can I reach for a decongestant spray? Dr Shantanu advises against self-medicating with them, because some cause rebound congestion when used longer than recommended. If symptoms are frequent, get them assessed instead of treating them again and again with over-the-counter medicines. Do fluids and sleep help? They support general wellbeing, and he recommends both. But they do not prevent pollution-related sinus inflammation on their own, so they belong beside the steps above, not instead of them. Delhi NCR's air pollution, driven by vehicle emissions, construction dust and smoke, can make breathing uncomfortable and aggravate existing nasal and sinus conditions. Photograph: ( Conway Airmen ) The goal of the whole routine is to reduce irritation and keep symptoms manageable, not to promise they will never appear. And home remedies? Warm compresses, rest, and saline rinses can ease a viral infection but cannot reliably clear a bacterial one. If symptoms continue, see a doctor. When to see an ENT specialist How do I know it has gone beyond a bad air day? Occasional sneezing often settles once you leave the trigger behind. Persistent or recurring symptoms deserve attention. Book a consultation if you have: congestion or facial pressure that will not improve repeated episodes of suspected sinusitis a persistent loss or reduction of smell blockage mainly on one side symptoms that disturb sleep or daily activities persistent or recurrent headache or ear heaviness What will the specialist do? An ENT specialist can tell pollution irritation apart from allergic rhinitis, recurrent sinusitis, nasal polyps or structural problems like a deviated septum. Saline nasal sprays and rinses can help clear mucus and trapped irritants, provided sterile, distilled or boiled-and-cooled water is used. Photograph: ( AI-Generated image ) That can mean reviewing your symptoms, exposure history and past treatments, examining your nasal passages, identifying allergy triggers, and advising on tests or imaging when clinically indicated. Treatment follows the cause, from saline irrigation to nasal medication or allergy management. Antibiotics are not routine for every episode, and surgery is for selected cases only. Which symptoms are urgent? Swelling or redness around the eyes, vision changes, a severe or unusual headache, confusion, or any rapidly worsening symptoms. Go to a doctor straight away. The one-breath version Check the AQI before you step out. Wear a snug N95 if you must. Keep indoor air clean. Rinse with safe water. Note whether your symptoms follow the smog. "None of this guarantees your sinuses will stay quiet. But if symptoms linger, recur or worsen, take that record to an ENT specialist. But most importantly, know that help is always available and self-medication is not a solution," Dr Shantanu says.

items.descriptionOriginal: On a Saturday morning in October 2026, seven Pune residents gathered at Madhavrao Scindia Garden beside the Mula River. Across the water, two fishers steered their boat past a thick patch of trees. The residents had brought smartphones and measuring tapes. They were there to document trees that people might pass every day without giving them much thought. They photographed individual trees, noted their species, measured the circumference of their trunks and recorded their locations on a phone app. Each entry added another piece to a growing map of Pune's riverbank greenery. It may seem like a small weekend exercise. But for these volunteers, knowing exactly which trees grow where could make a difference when the city decides what to build next. Why are Pune residents counting trees? The volunteers belong to Pune River Revival (PRR), a citizen group that began mapping trees more systematically in 2024, amid concerns about the ₹4,727-crore Pune Riverfront Development Project. The plan includes promenades, recreational spaces and other construction along the Mula-Mutha riverbanks. The group wanted a clearer record of the trees and other living things already thriving there. That meant going beyond counting trunks. "We started organizing the tree mapping exercise systematically in 2024," volunteer Raghunandan Patil told Mongabay. Earlier, he explained, the group had mapped trees by hand but lacked the technical knowledge to document them properly. Today, volunteers use iNaturalist, an app on which people can upload photographs and locations of plants and animals. It helps them identify species and build a record that others can consult. During mapping walks, volunteers spread out across stretches of the riverbank, taking photographs and measurements as they go. Every entry helps answer an important question: if a patch of greenery disappears tomorrow, will anyone know what was there? More than 500 trees faced removal. Residents got to work. That question became urgent on Ganeshkhind Road, where plans to widen a busy stretch threatened 529 trees , including mature trees believed to be decades old. When residents approached PRR, volunteers documented over 500 trees within a month. The records helped put names, numbers and locations to trees that people feared losing. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Pune Tree Mappers PRR (@punetreemapping.rivers) The concern spread beyond the mapping group. On 18 and 19 April 2026, residents, artists and environmentalists came together for tree mapping, live painting and music, drawing attention to the proposed widening of the road between Sancheti Hospital and Savitribai Phule Pune University. Under an earlier proposal, 469 trees were to be transplanted and 60 cut down. Environmentalists questioned whether older trees could survive being moved. "I grew up with these trees and they are part of every Punekar's heritage," artist Janaki Gandhi told Pune Mirror. "Through art, we want people to see each tree as a living identity, not just an obstacle in a road plan." Citizens also raised objections and pushed for changes to the road design. By September 2026, the Pune Municipal Corporation had revised its proposal, reducing the number of trees marked for removal from 529 to 33. That meant 496 trees could be spared under the revised plan. The change came through wider citizen action and efforts by environmental groups. Mapping helped document what was at stake and gave residents another way to make their case. What can a sacred grove teach a growing city? Along the rivers, PRR has also drawn attention to Ram-Mula Devrai, a sacred grove where the Ram and Mula rivers meet. A devrai is a forest patch traditionally protected by local communities because it is believed to be the dwelling place of a village deity. In a busy city, it can also offer shelter to plants, birds and other wildlife. Reports cited by Mongabay record around 1,000 heritage trees and at least 450 species of plants and animals in the grove. Among them are 160 bird species, as well as the Bengal monitor lizard and checkered keelback snake. During a mapping exercise, volunteers divide themselves across assigned stretches of the riverbank. Each person records observations directly on the platform. Photograph: (Pune River Revival-Via-Free Press Journal) To help more people discover this place, volunteers organised butterfly and insect walks, tree-painting competitions and other activities. They also suggested ways visitors could enjoy the space while protecting its trees. Their efforts showed how people could explore and appreciate a natural space while keeping its greenery intact. From riverbanks to hilltops, more people are joining in Elsewhere in Pune, citizens are building similar records. On Chatushrungi, Taljai and ARAI hills, the Green Hills Group uses an app called TrackMyTree to record saplings, their locations, species and caretakers. Revisiting those records can tell volunteers which trees are surviving and where they need attention. Along the Mula, PRR and JeevitNadi volunteers have also used ConnecTree, a tool developed by the Pune Knowledge Cluster, to document riverbank trees and saplings . View this post on Instagram A post shared by Civic Sense Task Force (CSTF) PCMC Pune (@civicsensetaskforce) Pune Municipal Corporation says it conducts a tree census every five years. But citizen groups believe accessible, regularly updated records are important too, especially when residents want to understand how a proposed project may affect their neighbourhood. Back at the river, the work still comes down to a photograph, a measurement and a location saved on a phone. The same simple steps the seven volunteers took that October morning could one day give residents a record to point to when an old tree is marked for removal. And as Pune continues to grow, these records give its residents something valuable: a clearer picture of the trees around them and a stronger voice in deciding how to protect them. Sources: 'How citizen scientists are mapping Pune's trees, with hopes of a greener future' : By Stephin Thomas, Published on 30 October 2026 'Pune Citizens Take Geotagging Of Green Cover Into Their Own Hands' : By Urban Acres, Published on 21 July 2025 'Citizens Launch Weekend Art and Music Protest to Save Ganeshkhind Road Trees' : By Chaitraly Deshmukh, Published on 18 April 2026

items.titleOriginal: A 22-Year-Old's Note on Unbecoming
items.description: Στα είκοσι δύο, ο Haile Thomas καθόταν με μια ερώτηση που οι περισσότεροι από εμάς κουβαλάμε ήσυχα για δεκαετίες: τι κάνω με όλη αυτή την ύπαρξη; Αντί να απαντήσει, έκανε κάτι πιο γενναίο -- έγραψε το δρόμο της στην ίδια την αβεβαιότητα. Ο προβληματισμός της δεν φτάνει ως συμβουλή αλλά ως άδεια: να νιώθει ημιτελής και ολοκληρωμένη ταυτόχρονα, να σταματήσει να περιμένει…
items.descriptionOriginal: At twenty-two, Haile Thomas sat with a question most of us quietly carry for decades: what do I do with all of this existence? Rather than answer it, she did something braver -- she wrote her way into the uncertainty itself. Her reflection arrives not as advice but as permission: to feel incomplete and whole at the same time, to stop waiting for the map that will never come. She offers a quietly radical image of identity -- that growing up is less about finding yourself than noticing "the entity that gets dressed," the spaciousness beneath every costume we try on and discard. There is no finish line in her telling, only transformations meeting us in the moments we least expect. "Growing up is a never ending journey," she writes -- and somehow that lands not as defeat but as relief. What she offers, finally, is not wisdom so much as weather: a loosening, a liquefying of the hard certainties we grip when life refuses to hold still.

items.descriptionOriginal: Μπορεί η ευτυχία να καλλιεργηθεί; Η περίπτωση του βουδιστή μοναχού Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche έχει κινήσει εδώ και χρόνια το ενδιαφέρον των νευροεπιστημόνων, καθώς μελέτες που εξέτασαν τον εγκέφαλό του κατά τη διάρκεια διαλογισμού κατέγραψαν εντυπωσιακά πρότυπα εγκεφαλικής δραστηριότητας. Συγκεκριμένα, οι απεικονίσεις έδειξαν ασυνήθιστα επίπεδα ενεργοποίησης στον αριστερό προμετωπιαίο φλοιό, μια περιοχή που σχετίζεται με θετικά συναισθήματα όπως η ευτυχία , ο ενθουσιασμός και η χαρά. Ο ίδιος δεν υπόσχεται κάποια εύκολη συνταγή. Αντίθετα, προτείνει να δοκιμάσουμε τα δικά του 9 μαθήματα ζωής, για μεγαλύτερη ικανοποίηση. Να μην προσπαθούμε να γεμίσουμε κάθε κενό Ένα από τα βασικά μηνύματα του Mingyur αφορά τη σύγχρονη ανάγκη για συνεχή διέγερση. «Όπως λέει ο Δαλάι Λάμα, σήμερα τα έχουμε όλα με το πάτημα ενός κουμπιού. Έτσι, όταν αρχίζουμε να νιώθουμε μοναξιά ή ανία, προσπαθούμε να προστατευτούμε με οτιδήποτε: παγωτό, κινητό, καφέ» , λέει χαρακτηριστικά στον Guardian. «Προσπαθούμε να ξεφύγουμε από αυτά τα συναισθήματα, όμως κατά κάποιον τρόπο κρύβουν σοφία. Το σημαντικό είναι να μείνουμε μαζί τους, να τα αποδεχτούμε και να τα χρησιμοποιήσουμε ως αφορμή για εξερεύνηση». Να αποδεχόμαστε τις αλλαγές Το 2011, ο Mingyur εγκατέλειψε το μοναστήρι του μέσα στη νύχτα, με σκοπό να ζήσει για ένα διάστημα ως περιπλανώμενος γιόγκι. Λίγες εβδομάδες αργότερα υπέστη σοβαρή τροφική δηλητηρίαση και πέρασε ημέρες εξαντλημένος από τον πόνο. Σήμερα περιγράφει εκείνη την εμπειρία ως καθοριστική για να κατανοήσει βαθύτερα την έννοια της εγκατάλειψης του ελέγχου. Όπως υποστηρίζει, δεν χρειάζεται κανείς να περάσει από μια ακραία δοκιμασία για να εξοικειωθεί με την αλλαγή. «Η σύγχρονη ζωή είναι γεμάτη περιπέτειες. Όταν γίνεσαι 18, όταν ξεκινάς μια νέα δουλειά ή μια νέα σχέση, όλα αυτά είναι ευκαιρίες για αλλαγή», λέει. Ακόμη και μικρές διαφοροποιήσεις στην καθημερινότητα, όπως μια νέα διαδρομή προς το σπίτι, μια διαφορετική δραστηριότητα ή μια καινούργια εμπειρία, μπορούν να βοηθήσουν κάποιον να γίνει πιο άνετος απέναντι στο άγνωστο. Δεν χρειαζόμαστε απαραίτητα σιωπή για να βρούμε γαλήνη Ο ίδιος παραδέχεται ότι όταν πρωτογνώρισε τον διαλογισμό , η αντίδρασή του κάθε άλλο παρά ενθουσιώδης ήταν. «Βαρέθηκα την πρώτη φορά που έμαθα διαλογισμό. Είπα: “Σήμερα αναπνοή. Αύριο πάλι αναπνοή. Όλη την υπόλοιπη εβδομάδα, αναπνοή. Αυτό είναι ανόητο”», θυμάται. Στη συνέχεια, όμως, κατανόησε ότι ο διαλογισμός δεν απαιτεί απαραίτητα απόλυτη ησυχία ή ιδανικές συνθήκες . «Για τον διαλογισμό χρειάζεται να ξέρεις δύο πράγματα. Πρώτον, μπορείς να διαλογιστείς οποτεδήποτε, οπουδήποτε, με οτιδήποτε. Δεύτερον, πρέπει να υπάρχει ένα δημιουργικό στοιχείο. Τα πάντα μπορούν να γίνουν φίλοι του διαλογισμού». Αυτό σημαίνει ότι ακόμη και ο θόρυβος της κίνησης, μια συζήτηση στο διπλανό δωμάτιο ή άλλοι περισπασμοί μπορούν να γίνουν σημεία εστίασης αντί για εμπόδια. Να αξιοποιήσουμε 3 βασικούς πυλώνες Ο Mingyur περιγράφει τρεις βασικούς άξονες της θιβετιανής βουδιστικής παράδοσης: οπτική, διαλογισμό και εφαρμογή . «Η οπτική είναι η νοοτροπία. Πιστεύουμε ότι όλοι έχουν έναν εσωτερικό ουρανό, τις ποιότητες της επίγνωσης, της αγάπης, της συμπόνιας και της σοφίας. Εξασκούμε τον διαλογισμό και μετά εφαρμόζουμε όσα μάθαμε, χτίζοντας νέες συνήθειες», εξηγεί. Για τον ίδιο, η αλλαγή της οπτικής απαιτεί εξάσκηση. «Είναι εύκολο να πει κανείς “οι άνθρωποι δεν είναι καλοί”. Υπάρχουν όμως πολλές σπουδαίες ιδιότητες σε πολλούς ανθρώπους. Αν αρχίσεις να τις βλέπεις, θα εμφανίζονται περισσότερο. Είναι συνήθεια: πρέπει να το κάνεις ξανά και ξανά και τότε αλλάζεις». Μια απλή καθημερινή άσκηση θα μπορούσε να είναι η συνειδητή αναγνώριση θετικών χαρακτηριστικών στους ανθρώπους γύρω μας, ακόμα και σε εκείνους που μας ενοχλούν περισσότερο. Να νιώθουμε ευγνωμοσύνη, αλλά όχι γενικά και αόριστα Η ευγνωμοσύνη, σύμφωνα με τον Mingyur, δεν χρειάζεται να παίρνει τη μορφή μιας γενικής λίστας. «Εκτιμώ ότι έχω τις αισθήσεις μου, ότι υπάρχει μια στέγη πάνω από το κεφάλι μου, ότι έχω τουλάχιστον έναν ή δύο φίλους ή συγγενείς» , λέει. «Όταν αρχίσουμε να εκτιμούμε αυτά τα πράγματα, αρχίζουμε να εκτιμούμε την ποιότητα της ζωής μας και όλα όσα υπάρχουν γύρω μας». Η ουσία βρίσκεται στο συγκεκριμένο: σε μια άνετη καρέκλα, σε μια ήρεμη στιγμή, σε μια καθημερινή εικόνα που συνήθως περνά απαρατήρητη. Να θυμόμαστε ότι ο πανικός είναι μόνο ένα σύννεφο στον ουρανό Ο μοναχός μιλά και για τις κρίσεις πανικού που είχε σε νεαρή ηλικία. «Όταν άρχισα να μαθαίνω διαλογισμό από τον πατέρα μου, τον ρώτησα πώς να τις πολεμήσω. Μου είπε: “Μην πολεμάς”», θυμάται. Όπως εξηγεί, η προσπάθεια να διώξει κάποιος τον φόβο μπορεί να τον ενισχύσει. «Δεν χρειάζεται να διώξω τον πανικό. Είναι σαν σύννεφο καταιγίδας στον ουρανό. Έρχεται και φεύγει, χωρίς να αλλάζει τον ουρανό. Πρέπει απλώς να συνδεθείς με τον εσωτερικό σου ουρανό». Σε στιγμές έντασης, προτείνει να στρέφουμε την προσοχή σε απτές αισθήσεις, όπως η θερμοκρασία ή οι ήχοι γύρω μας. Και ο θυμός η πάχνη στο γρασίδι «Αυτό που αποκαλούμε επίγνωση είναι σαν το φως του ήλιου και τα συναισθηματικά μας μοτίβα είναι σαν την πάχνη στο γρασίδι το πρωί. Όταν εμφανίζεται το φως του ήλιου, η πάχνη λιώνει αυτόματα. Δεν υπάρχει μάχη» τονίζει. Η πρότασή του είναι απλή: Πριν αντιδράσουμε, να αναγνωρίσουμε πρώτα το συναίσθημα. « Μείνε με τον θυμό . Έστω για ένα δευτερόλεπτο. Μόλις τον πιάσεις, έχεις επιλογή. Μπορεί να μεταμορφωθεί». Να μην περιμένουμε την ευτυχία στην επόμενη επιτυχία Για τον Mingyur, το κυνήγι της ευτυχίας μπορεί εύκολα να οδηγήσει στο αντίθετο αποτέλεσμα . «Η γνήσια ευτυχία έρχεται όταν αφήνουμε αυτό το αίσθημα δυσαρέσκειας, ανεπάρκειας, ότι κάτι λείπει», λέει. «Οι άνθρωποι συχνά σκέφτονται: “Θα είμαι ευτυχισμένος αν βγάλω περισσότερα χρήματα, αν μετακομίσω σε μια νέα χώρα, αν βρω μια νέα δουλειά ή αν κερδίσω το λαχείο”. Όμως αυτό αλλάζει την ευτυχία μόνο λίγο και μετά επιστρέφεις στο βασικό επίπεδο». Κατά τον ίδιο, πρακτικές όπως η συνειδητή αναπνοή, η αγάπη και η συμπόνια μπορούν σταδιακά να επηρεάσουν αυτή τη βασική αίσθηση ευεξίας . Και, τελικά, βοηθά να βοηθάμε Στο τέλος, ο Mingyur επιστρέφει σε μια πολύ απλή ιδέα: η ευτυχία δεν είναι μόνο εσωτερική υπόθεση. «Αν μπορείς πραγματικά να βοηθήσεις τους άλλους, νιώθεις ένα διαφορετικό επίπεδο ευτυχίας από αυτό που μπορεί να σου δώσει ένα παγωτό ή ένας καφές», καταλήγει. Διαβάστε επίσης Ευτυχία: Μία ψυχολόγος δίνει 5 πολύτιμες συμβουλές για να νιώσουμε χαρά όταν όλα γύρω μας είναι ζοφερά Θλίψη και αίσθημα κενού: Τι είναι το σύνδρομο της «άδειας ζωής» και πώς θα το διαχειριστούμε Γιατί το εμμονικό κυνήγι της ευτυχίας γίνεται μπούμερανγκ που εξουθενώνει και οδηγεί σε δυστυχία

items.descriptionOriginal: Low oxygen levels in the brain, or cerebral anoxia, are a leading cause of death worldwide. Patients who recover from cerebral anoxia deal with persistent neurological issues that worsen their quality of life. Building on previous work showing that brain–heart interactions can predict the severity of symptoms and survival, Diego Candia-Rivera, Sofia Carrion-Falgarona and colleagues from the Paris Brain Institute assessed whether brain–heart interactions in a rat model of severe oxygen loss can predict survival after resuscitation. The work is published in eNeuro.

items.descriptionOriginal: An Indian Village with ZERO Electricity Bill, FREE Cooking Gas & Women Own Every Home? Sounds like a fairytale? Meet Shelkewadi, Maharashtra! For 20+ years, Shelkewadi has solved problems that Indian cities still struggle with: LPG dependency, power cuts, water crisis, pollution, and waste, all without crores in budget. In this episode of Solved In India, we visit this tiny village in Karvir Taluka, Kolhapur, where barely 80 families live. They’ve built a real-life zero-waste, self-sufficient, sustainable village model that every Indian village can copy. With 60% of India’s LPG imported and a big part of it passing through the Strait of Hormuz, Shelkewadi shows what energy independence looks like at the village level. Imagine if every village in India followed this model. Would you move to a village like this? items.descriptionOriginal: A stick figure family, a googly-eyed monster, a happy rainbow. Children’s artwork represents how they see the world at any given age — a sweet, fleeting perspective that the adults in their lives yearn to preserve. But kids are prolific creators, so what’s to be done with all these construction paper canvases as more continuously flood in? Artist Shana Blakley came up with a creative way to save her kids’ drawings while breaking out of a rut she’d been in with her own work: She turned them into a big, colorful collage to hang in her family’s home. When she shared the result on Instagram, her comment section exploded. The idea clearly resonated with other moms, dads, and grandparents. Heirloom Collage Shana Blakley’s first kids’ artwork collage “We want to honor what our kids make,” Blakley told Nice News, adding: “Nearly every parent around the world has a growing pile of kid art, and it’s in our nature to save it. We feel guilty throwing it away, but storing it also begins to feel unsettling. There comes a time when you realize how much of it you have and you ask yourself: ‘What am I keeping this for?’” Heirloom Collage Molly Revers with her grandkids and the collages made from their artwork Shortly after posting the piece last year, she launched Heirloom Collage and started taking commissions. Now, she offers an online course that guides participants in producing their own artist-quality collages out of kiddos’ creations. The course consists of six video modules totaling one hour, and Blakley provides feedback in a private Facebook group where students can post their in-progress and completed work. Molly Revers enjoys dabbling in different artistic endeavors, so she signed up for the $99 e-course. “The most meaningful aspect was the joy it brought me when creating the collages and the joy it brought my little grandsons when they saw their work displayed in such a cool way,” she shared. “They love picking their favorite creations and memories associated with them.” Heirloom Collage Another parent’s completed collage For Blakley, who lives in Richmond, Virginia, and began her career as a fine artist over a decade ago, the project reconnected her to a sense of spontaneity after a period of creative stagnation. “Halfway through it, I recall thinking, ‘[My kids] didn’t second-guess their creativity in these pieces, so I shouldn’t either,’” she said. “That was a big breakthrough for me.” It’s something many adults, artists or not, can relate to. “A lot of my students haven’t made art since they were kids, and this brings them back to it,” Blakley added. Overall, though, the memorable shared experience of making that first collage with her two children — the youngsters helped select the included drawings and “were buzzing with pride” — is what she wishes for her clients. “That connection is what lasts, and they end up with something their family really treasures,” she said. Heirloom Collage Jeanine Long-Tuohy with her granddaughter Ava and the collage they made Jeanine Long-Tuohy, who loves her granddaughter Ava’s artwork, created her first piece with Ava’s help and has since started a new one with another grandchild. “Working on this made me feel like there’s a lot more we can do together,” Long-Tuohy said. “It’s a memory they will always have of me.”

items.title: Το 1997, οι Blur ηχογράφησαν ένα τραγούδι διάρκειας 2 λεπτών για να κάνουν φάρσα στη δισκογραφική τους εταιρεία. Έγινε ύμνος της δεκαετίας του '90.
items.titleOriginal: In 1997, Blur recorded a 2-minute song to prank their record label. It became a ’90s anthem.
items.description: Το "Song 2" του Blur είναι βασικός πυλώνας σε αθλητικές εκδηλώσεις και σε ταινίες δράσης για σχεδόν 30 χρόνια, με τις απίστευτες κιθάρες, την εμβληματική εισαγωγή των ντραμς και το ακαταμάχητα απλό ρεφρέν "Woo-hoo". Αν και οι Blur είχαν την ικανότητα να γράφουν απίστευτα πιασάρικες μελωδίες, το μεγαλύτερο μέρος της μουσικής τους, μέχρι το 1997, ήταν το Indie rock που έκλινε σε κοινωνικά σχόλια για τη σύγχρονη βρετανική…
items.descriptionOriginal: “Song 2” by Blur has been a mainstay at sporting events and in action movies for nearly 30 years, with its blazing guitars, iconic drum intro, and irresistibly simple “Woo-hoo” chorus. Although Blur had a knack for writing incredibly catchy tunes , most of their music, up to 1997, was Indie rock that leaned into social commentary on modern British life . Not the kinda stuff you’d hear over a loudspeaker at a Dallas Cowboys game. By 1997, the band was moving away from Britpop, a genre it helped define, which celebrated an over-the-top, cartoony Britishness, sneered at the Americanization of UK culture, and stood in opposition to grunge rock. When the band hit the studio to record its 5th album, the eponymous Blur , they did an about-face. The band began taking cues from its former enemies across the pond, embracing American noise rock and hip-hop. Blur’s ‘Song 2’ began very differently Damon Albarn, the band’s singer and primary songwriter, brought a goofy song to one of their sessions: an acoustic bossa nova with a chorus that had a whistle like a cat-call or, as they say in the UK, a “wolf whistle.” Here’s what the original “Song 2” sounded like: When Blur’s guitarist Graham Coxon heard the song, he told Albarn , “That’s too f***ing nice,” and proposed something entirely different. “I was like, ‘Let’s do it really fast, really noisy, and really horrible, and tell the record label we want to record it as a single. It’ll scare them to death. They’ll hate it,'” Coxon told Produce Like a Pro . The band rearranged the song with a quiet verse and an extremely loud chorus, reminiscent of American grunge rock, the sound that the band rebelled against for most of their career. By embracing the big, dumb, quiet-loud-quiet sound of grunge, the band was, as the English say, taking the piss from the dying grunge genre. The band recorded the song with guitars cranked to 11 and doubled the fuzzy bass guitar at the end. Coxon joined drummer Dave Rowntree by tapping his stick on the floor tom and adding an extra tom during the verses, giving it an off-kilter feel. Albarn recorded a scratch vocal with nonsense lyrics he intended to rerecord later. But he realized that he couldn’t recreate the feeling he had on the original vocals, so they stayed on the track. “I got my head checked by a jumbo jet.” What does it mean? Could it be a Beastie Boys reference? The album Licensed to Ill featured a jumbo jet crashing into a mountain, and the name of the group’s third album is Check Your Head ? The song was named “Song 2” because it was 2 minutes and 2 seconds long and would be the second track on the album. Blur’s joke didn’t go as intended After the band played the song for their record label, their joke backfired. The label loved the song. “They came in, and we played it to them giggling, and they were like, ‘Wow, this is excellent,’” Coxon recalled . “Song 2” would be a massive hit in the US, UK, and across Europe, and a high point in Blur’s relationship with America, where its quintessential Englishness had been a barrier to breaking into the mainstream. The band would grow a larger following in the U.S. over the years, after Albarn’s musical second act, Gorillaz, fared much better stateside. In 2018, Coxon joined Albarn’s Gorillaz on stage at a show outside of Los Angeles for a “Song 2” cover that brought their career full circle. Woo-hoo, indeed. The post In 1997, Blur recorded a 2-minute song to prank their record label. It became a ’90s anthem. appeared first on Upworthy .

Πολλοί υποθέτουν αυτή την επικοινωνία…
items.descriptionOriginal: The funny thing about social intelligence is that it’s a major factor in how successful we are in relationships, careers, and managing our mental health. We shape children’s behavior to follow social norms, but most parents don’t teach them how to make small talk, handle rude people, or how long to hold eye contact. Many assume these communication habits are innate, but people with great communication and interpersonal skills aren’t just born that way; they often hone their skills like an athlete or musician. The good news is that almost anyone can improve their communication skills with a little practice. A man giving a speech. Credit: Canva Recently, a Redditor asked people on the Answers forum to share the tricks they use in social situations. “What is a social ‘cheat code’ that completely changes how people treat you?” they asked, and they received nearly 1,000 responses; many shared good advice on handling rude people or improving their likability. Here are 15 of the best social ‘cheat codes’ in the thread. 1. Let them think they’re smart “People are easier to manipulate if you let them believe that they’re smarter than you.” “Ahh, yes, the Columbo Method.” 2. Lose weight “The difference in how people treat you when you’re thin vs fat is astounding. When I first lost weight around 22, it caused me a lot of anger & resentment because of the huge difference in attitudes & attraction people suddenly had towards me. When I got older & put weight back on, I also noticed how I slowly became invisible again & people treated it like an inconvenience if they had to interact with me.” “Can confirm this to be true. I accidentally lost two stone and had an INSANE time for like six months being skinny as sh*t. People treated me very differently, men and women. Men were suddenly very interested in me. The number of compliments I got was baffling. My sex life was on fire for a year.” 3. Be polite “I would add that politeness delivered in an assured and confident manner is far more powerful than a weak one, the latter comes across more as insecurity and submissive.” People politely bowing to each other. Credit: Canva 4. Don’t trash talk “Seriously. No matter how much you dislike someone, there’s zero value to be gained speaking ill of others. Just avoid them if you don’t like them. But trash talking always gets back to people and invites nothing else other than problems.” Experts agree that when people gossip or talk trash about others behind their back, it reflects poorly on them. A study in the European Journal of Social Psychology found that gossipers are seen as less powerful and those who spread more negative gossip than positive are less likable. Another study from the Journal of Experimental Social Psychology found that people are less likely to go to gossipers for advice because they don’t trust them with their problems. 5. Be interested, not interesting “Be genuinely interested in other people rather than trying to convince other people to be interested in you. People are constantly looking for excuses to talk about themselves. Let them. They love it.” “I get so much mileage from this at work, and coworkers are continually puzzled why my rapport with other teams is so good. They don’t notice I’m asking about if the kids have gotten over the flu, about the boardgames I saw behind them on video, ask what their favorite part of their vacation was. I know everybody’s hobbies, I put operation dates in my calendar, and so on.” This was one of Dale Carnegie’s core teachings in the communications classic, How to Win Friends & Influence People . Carnegie said, “To be interesting, be interested,” meaning that there is no greater gift you can give someone than your interest and attention. People love talking about themselves, so if you ask people great follow-up questions, they will like you more than if you wowed them with your great stories and wit. 6. When they’re rude, be nice “Ask gentle questions to rude remarks. ‘What did you mean by that?’ Asked earnestly.” “I do exactly that. It’s actually fun to see what the reaction will be. People are so caught off guard.” 7. Be pleased to see them “Appear to be genuinely, honestly, pleased to see them. Don’t be fake and effusive about it. Don’t act like you would if you were unexpectedly seeing a good friend you haven’t seen in months; act like you would upon seeing a good friend you saw yesterday and knew you’d see today. Just glad they’re here.” “Act like you would upon seeing a good friend you saw yesterday and knew you’d see today. Just glad they’re here.” 8. Give genuine compliments “People will like you if you make them feel good about themselves. Look for opportunities to give genuine compliments and build other people up.” “I’m in and out of offices all day for work and if I’m having a bum day, I’ll compliment someone else. ‘I like your sweater’ ‘that whatever looks great’ ‘oh you got a new blank, it’s awesome!’ Totally benign things, really. I’m not lying when I say I like their stuff or whatever, but I can tell it makes them feel good and that brightens my mood.” 9. Get a dog “Get a dog. In the UK at least it feels like a cheat code to social engagement.” “So much. It’s like a secret club just opens up and beckons you in, isn’t it?” A woman walking her dog. Credit: Canva 10. Respect everyone “Treat everyone you meet as a respected equal. Respect should not be ‘earned’. It should be the default and only ‘lost’, not gained.” “You’ll be surprised how much people in positions that gets shat on really appreciate this. I can speak from both sides of the equation. Where there is a structural power imbalance where someone does need to be nice but does anyway, it makes a big difference.” 11. Dress nicely “I think that looking dressed-up and stylish is the biggest cheat code. I think people treat you better and assume you are smarter if you look well-coiffed.” “Doesn’t have to be mainstream fashion either. This works for subcultures as well.” 12. Wear a beanie “If you work customer service and wear a beanie people will act way more goofy and human and real with you. It’s just a correlation I’ve noticed.” “Wow good call, never thought. Any hat that’s not a ball cap would have me drop my guard I think.” 13. Notice their eye color “I have a really hard time with eye contact. When talking to strangers at work (retail), I try to notice what color each person’s eyes are. It makes a huge difference in how they respond and treat me.” If you’re uncomfortable making contact, another popular technique is the “Triangle Method.” After making eye contact, slowly move your gaze to their eyebrows (in a professional setting), or their nose (in a social setting). This makes it look as though you’re maintaining eye contact, when in reality, you’re taking a break from time to time. 14. Ask for a favor “Ask for a small favor. Thank them effusively. Express gratitude one more time either in the next conversation or in front of another person. You have made them feel amazing about themselves for being nice to you. You now have a friend for life.” 15. Take responsibility “Actually taking responsibility for your actions, mistakes, successes. This includes your reactions and responses to those situations, statements and people which might offend you. This is an incredibly empowering practice in life. It takes a lot of work and of introspection, but is so worth it, confidence goes up and people tend to respect your honesty and humility.” The post People swear these 15 psychological ‘cheat codes’ improve how you’re treated in social situations appeared first on Upworthy .

items.title: Έχασε τη δουλειά του και άρχισε να κόβει γρασίδι δωρεάν. Τώρα 2.100 εθελοντές έχουν ενταχθεί μαζί του.
items.titleOriginal: He lost his job and started mowing lawns for free. Now 2,100 volunteers have joined him.
items.description: Όταν ο Brian Schwartz απολύθηκε το 2020, ακριβώς στη σφοδρότητα της πανδημίας COVID-19, όλα ήταν ανάποδα. Εκτός από το ότι έχασε τη δουλειά του, ήταν νέος πατέρας που φρόντιζε επίσης έναν άρρωστο γονέα. Συν τοις άλλοις, όλος ο κόσμος ένιωθε αβέβαιος και αδέσμευτος με τρόπο που κανένας μας δεν είχε βιώσει ποτέ. Θα μπορούσε κανείς να καθίσει στο σπίτι και να βουτήξει σε τέτοιο γ…
items.descriptionOriginal: When Brian Schwartz got laid off in 2020, right in the thick of the COVID-19 pandemic , everything was upside down. In addition to losing his job, he was a new father who was also caring for a sick parent. On top of that, the whole world felt uncertain and unmoored in a way none of us had ever experienced. One could sit at home and wallow in such circumstances. But Schwartz took another tack; he looked outside of himself to see where he could help someone else. He noticed some elderly neighbors needed help with their yards and figured that was a safe, socially distanced way to offer some service. Now, that single idea has blossomed into a full-fledged, award-winning network of 2,100 volunteers. Neighbors helping neighbors, in every state in the nation. And it’s still growing. On Day 4 of #HOPEWeek , we recognized Brian Schwartz and his national non-profit, "I Want To Mow Your Lawn" Originated during the pandemic, @IWTMYL provides older adults, veterans, and neighbors facing physical or financial hardship with free, temporary lawn care relief… pic.twitter.com/1aQkHG822X — New York Yankees (@Yankees) June 18, 2026 How I Want to Mow Your Lawn works for volunteers Schwartz named the organization I Want to Mow Your Lawn . Here’s how it works on the volunteer side: Volunteers can sign up and offer yard services in their local areas. You don’t need special training or equipment—you just offer whatever services you can do. And if you only have equipment to offer, you can either loan or donate it through the organization’s Pay It Forward marketplace , “We sometimes work with lawn care creators and even professional landscapers, but most of our volunteers are everyday neighbors,” Schwartz explains. He also makes the expectation clear that each volunteer service is a one-time offering, not an ongoing promise or commitment (which would be a lot more complicated to manage). “We offer temporary relief when someone nearby is available, and we can’t guarantee a visit or ongoing service,” he explains. Schwartz shares that I Want to Mow Your Lawn has tried to make connections with neighbors as easy as possible: “Volunteers can get alerts about nearby requests and call or text homeowners without sharing their personal phone numbers. Our Buddy System lets volunteers team up, and churches, workplaces and other groups can organize a service day .” He says volunteers have made more than 3,100 free service visits so far. How it works for recipients Those with a yard service need have multiple avenues for getting matched up with a volunteer. The website has an online intake form, but that isn’t always the easiest route for seniors. “About a third of requests come through our phone line, 862-66-MOWER, because many of the people who need us aren’t online,” Schwartz explains. “They can leave a message in their own words, and we get it to volunteers nearby. More than 100 case managers and social workers have also referred people to us.” Schwartz points out that it’s not just an aesthetic need being filled in many cases. Overgrown yards can also be trip hazards for elderly folks. “Two AARP Community Challenge grants this year are also helping us make homes and streets safer for older residents,” he says. “That’s another part of what this has grown into. Yard work can be about being able to get around your home safely, too.” Beyond the lawn: An Air Force veteran gets an extra surprise When Schwartz first started mowing lawns for free, he focused on elderly neighbors and veterans. For Veterans Day this year, he got to do something extra special for a veteran named Marcy alongside two other generous lawncare legends. “I teamed up with lawn care creators Nathan’s Lawns and Gardens from Australia and Kyle Breiner of Breiner Lawn from Ohio right here in New Jersey to transform an Air Force veteran’s yard,” he told Upworthy. (This was Nathan’s fifth trip to the U.S., where he knocks on doors and cleans up yards for free. Honda sponsored the trip and provided the tools.) Marcy served in the U.S. Air Force, but has faced struggles in her life since. She became homeless with her children after leaving a domestic violence situation. Her granddaughter has medical needs and lives in Texas, so she doesn’t get to see her very often in person. Watch: View this post on Instagram In addition to the $200 on the spot, Nathan launched a GoFundMe for Marcy, which has raised over $3,000 AUD (around $2,000 USD) as of the writing of this article. (Fundraisers for the people he helps have led to Nathan being named one of GoFundMe’s “The Kind 50” fundraisers. You can find the GoFundMe for Marcy here to show her some extra love.) Providing volunteer lawn care has truly become a widespread group effort, as Schwartz stays connected with other like-minded individuals and organizations. For example, Rodney Smith, Jr. (aka The Lawnmower Man, whom Upworthy has written about before), is a resource partner for I Want to Mow Your Lawn. “Rodney focuses a lot on engaging younger generations, including elementary school students, while we’re working primarily with adults and handling the end-to-end process of connecting volunteers with people who need help,” Schwartz says. “There’s quite a bit happening behind the scenes on the technology side, too, including automation to help make those connections easier and more efficient. As we both like to say, there’s still plenty of grass to mow!” The need still outweighs the supply of volunteers—and you can help There is, indeed, plenty of grass to mow. In fact, in the past year, requests for I Want to Mow Your Lawn services have nearly doubled. “From January 1 through November 10 this year, we received 7,049 requests for help, and 679 new volunteers signed up,” Schwartz shares. “Having volunteers in every state doesn’t mean we have someone in every neighborhood.” The need is real. “At our busiest point this summer, we received more than 60 requests a day,” Schwartz explains. “About half of those asking are 65 or older, roughly three in four report a disability or physical limitation, and about one in seven are veterans.” Still, the volunteer numbers are growing. “We have more than 2,100 approved volunteers across all 50 states now, people willing to give their own time for someone they’ve never met,” Schwartz says. “That still gets me.” Schwartz is back to full-time work now and runs I Want to Mow Your Lawn in his free time. He says it works well because “it’s something people can actually do.” Even the Yankees can do it: View this post on Instagram “You don’t have to solve everything in someone’s life to take one thing off their shoulders,” he says. “A caregiver in Arizona once wrote to me (she posted a review on our Facebook page) after a group of volunteers cleared an overgrown yard: ‘Brian I thank you for giving James the sky back.’ That says it better than I can.” “I’m proud of how far this has come and grateful to everyone who helped build it,” he adds. “At the same time, I read the stories coming in and think about the people we haven’t been able to reach. It’s hard knowing someone needs help and having to be honest that we can’t promise it. That’s what keeps me motivated to keep building this. We’ve made a difference, and there’s still a lot of work to do.” Check out the I Want to Mow Your Lawn website to learn how to volunteer in your neighborhood. The post He lost his job and started mowing lawns for free. Now 2,100 volunteers have joined him. appeared first on Upworthy .

items.description: Τον Δεκέμβριο του 2003, δύο οικογένειες σε γειτονικές πολιτείες ζούσαν αντίθετους εφιάλτες. Στο Κεντάκι, ο 18 μηνών Μπρούκλιν Ντότσον πέθαινε. Μια σπάνια πάθηση του ήπατος της είχε αφήσει τις μέρες του θανάτου της χωρίς μεταμόσχευση και στο Οχάιο, ο 10χρονος Μάικλ Γουότερς είχε μόλις χτυπηθεί και σκοτωθεί από ένα αυτοκίνητο. Ο Μάικλ είχε πει στην οικογένειά του ότι ήθελε να γίνει α…
items.descriptionOriginal: In December 2003, two families in neighboring states were living through opposite nightmares . In Kentucky, 18-month-old Brooklyn Dotson was dying. A rare liver condition had left her days from death without a transplant, and in Ohio, 10-year-old Michael Waters had just been struck and killed by a car . Michael had told his family he wanted to be an organ donor, and they honored that wish. His liver went to Brooklyn, who received the transplant at Cincinnati Children’s Hospital. “Even as a kid, he’d do anything for anybody,” his younger brother, Noah Waters, told LEX 18 . “He was a sweet kid. Probably he was way more mature than he needed to be.” The two families met in person in 2005 and stayed in touch over the years. Brooklyn and Noah, who was five years younger than his late brother, became close friends. He was there for her when she needed another surgery as a teenager. Then, in 2025, things shifted. Brooklyn realized her feelings for Noah had changed, and her mom let him know. That weekend, he drove from Ohio to Kentucky to tell her he had always felt the same way. “It got to the point we were FaceTiming each other 8 hours a day,” Brooklyn said. Noah proposed on Christmas Eve. On Sept. 26, they were married overlooking Lake Cumberland in Kentucky, and Brooklyn took the Waters name. “I was crying all day,” Noah told People . He believes his brother was looking out for him from heaven. He’s also clear-eyed about how unusual their path was. “I’d say he probably knew what his purpose was,” he told LEX 18. “I had no idea that my brother was gonna save my wife’s life 20 years later.” For her part, Brooklyn says she hopes the attention raises awareness about organ donation. “I get to enjoy life because of him, and I get to live and hopefully honor his memory the best way that I can,” she said. The post A 10-year-old boy’s liver saved her life when she was a baby. She just married his little brother. appeared first on Upworthy .

items.title: Το Peacock εισβάλλει στο σπίτι του ζευγαριού μόνο και μόνο για να κοιταχτεί στον καθρέφτη. Στη συνέχεια οδηγεί ολόκληρη τη γειτονιά σε μια εβδομαδιαία καταδίωξη.
items.titleOriginal: Peacock breaks into couple’s house just to look in the mirror. Then he leads entire neighborhood on a weeklong chase.
items.description: Ο Geoff και η Delwyn Ballantyne βγήκαν μόνο για έναν βραδινό καφέ. Όταν επέστρεψαν στο σπίτι τους στο Alexandra Hills, ένα προάστιο του Μπρίσμπεϊν της Αυστραλίας, ένα αρσενικό παγώνι βρισκόταν στο μπάνιο τους και κοιτούσε τον εαυτό του στον καθρέφτη της ματαιοδοξίας. «Υπήρχαν πολλές κραυγές από τη γυναίκα μου», είπε ο Geoff στον Guardian. «Σκέφτηκε ότι πρέπει να υπήρχε κάποιος εισβολέας…
items.descriptionOriginal: Geoff and Delwyn Ballantyne only stepped out for an evening coffee . When they returned to their home in Alexandra Hills, a suburb of Brisbane, Australia, a male peacock was in their bathroom, gazing at himself in the vanity mirror . “There was a lot of screaming from my wife,” Geoff told The Guardian . “She thought there must have been an intruder, but then she says it’s a peacock. I did believe her, but I tried not to, because it wasn’t very believable.” They tried to tempt him away with water and crackers, but he wouldn’t leave the mirror. Wildlife rescuers eventually wrapped him in a towel and released him into nearby bushland. But he didn’t stay there. The peacock started showing up every afternoon at the acreage property of another Alexandra Hills resident, Suzie Tafolo, who suspected he belonged to a local tattoo artist, Elliot Ross. Ross had been searching for his missing peacock, Hex, and confirmed from photos that the bathroom intruder was him. Then Tafolo did some research. “I’ve Googled how to catch a peacock, which is something I never thought I’d have to do,” she said. “One of the things it says is that they love mirrors, which makes sense in terms of how he ended up in the bathroom.” So she hauled a full-length mirror out to the shed where Hex kept turning up. The mirror probably wasn’t about vanity. Urban ecologist Darryl Jones told The Guardian that most birds read their reflection as another bird, and Hex may simply have been drawn to what looked like company. Ross had his own theory. “We’ve got a female here as well, and she’s stayed,” he said. “I’m guessing he’s gone walkabout trying to find another female.” There are also a bunch of videos online showing confused peacocks attacking themselves in the mirror. Meanwhile, Hex became a neighborhood project, with hundreds of locals tracking his sightings on social media. A week after the bathroom incident, they cornered him in a backyard and used blankets to block his escape. Then, family friend Jordy Barker “just dived in and grabbed him by his legs. He was going ballistic, but she held on,” Ross said. “I haven’t caught a peacock before, but I used to live on a farm and had to catch turkeys and chickens all the time,” Barker said. “It was just like catching a turkey.” Hex’s return home came with a scare. He had picked up about half a dozen ticks on the run, and his owners rushed him to a 24-hour vet, where he was treated with an antiserum normally used for dogs. He responded well and is now back home with the family’s peahen, Nyx. Ross had actually been planning to bring home another female that weekend. “I guess we were too late,” he said. items.titleOriginal: Gen Z woman who went viral for being burned out after one day at ‘grown-up’ job gets laid off
items.description: Κάθε χρόνο, μια νέα γενιά ενηλίκων συνειδητοποιεί πόσο δύσκολο είναι να είσαι πραγματικά ενήλικας. Δεν είναι πολλά πράγματα που μπορούν να σας προετοιμάσουν σωστά για τις ευθύνες και τα προβλήματα που αντιμετωπίζετε ως ανεξάρτητος άνθρωπος στο εργατικό δυναμικό. Η TikToker Brielle Asero, η οποία ήταν 21 ετών τότε και πρόσφατα απόφοιτος κολεγίου, έγινε viral στο TikTok για τη συναισθηματική της αντίδραση…
items.descriptionOriginal: Every year, a new generation of adults realizes how hard it is to actually be an adult. Not many things can properly prepare you for the responsibilities and problems you face being an independent human being in the work force . TikToker Brielle Asero, who was 21 at the time and a recent college graduate, went viral on TikTok for her emotional reaction to the first day at a 9-to-5 job. The video, which received over 3.4 million views, captured the public’s attention because it was like a cultural Rorschach test. Some who saw the video thought that Asero came off as entitled and exemplified the younger generation’s lack of work ethic. In contrast, others sympathized with the young woman who is just beginning to understand how hard it is to find work-life balance in modern-day America . Here is what she actually said in the video “I’m so upset,” she says in the video. “I get on the train at 7:30 a.m., and I don’t get home until 6:15 p.m. [at the] earliest. I don’t have time to do anything!” “I don’t have the time to do anything,” she continued. “I want to shower, eat my dinner, and go to sleep. I don’t have the time or energy to cook my dinner either. I don’t have energy to work out, like, that’s out of the window. I’m so upset, oh my god.” @brielleybelly123 im also getting sick leave me alone im emotional ok i feel 12 and im scared of not having time to live ♬ original sound – BRIELLE Then two months later, she got laid off On December 16, 2023, Asero gave an update on her professional life, and sadly, things aren’t going too well. After just 2 months on the job, she was laid off. It had taken her 5 months to find the job and she had recently relocated to New York City to be near the office. “I worked for a startup, and they didn’t have the workload or the bandwidth they needed to train me and to give me work to do,” she said. Being laid off during the holidays makes Asero’s situation even more difficult because most employers are closed for business in late December and early January. Remember, laid off does not mean fired. Asero had some stern words for those who would blame her for losing her job. “I know that I’m a hard worker, and my boss literally said that I’m one of the smartest people he’s ever had working under him, and he knows that I’m going to land on my feet, and he will give me a great referral to anybody, so don’t start,” she warned. @brielleybelly123 can someone tell me im going to be okay !!!! feels like the world is ending i need a job immediatley i am feeling so lost rn like i moved for this…!? ♬ original sound – BRIELLE “I have done everything I possibly could have, and it’s still not enough,” she said. To supplement her income while looking for her next big break, Asero says she will look for work as a server or nanny. Even though Asero took a lot of criticism for crying after her first day at work, the comments on the new video were overwhelmingly positive and supportive. There were also a lot of people who shared how they had recently been laid off, too. Her first experience in the workforce was a hard one, but her reaction to it was completely valid and something we’ve all felt before. “Just want to note that there’s no shame in taking a service job while you’re still looking. You’re going to be okay, you got this,” Baby bel wrote. “It happened to me, seems like ur life is ending, but I promise it’s just getting started. You’ll laugh about it at some point,” Rachie added. So where is Brielle now? These days, Brielle is doing alright for herself in New York City. Among other things, she has a thriving career as a content creator with over 700k followers on TikTok. That job and the heartbreaking experience of getting laid off, it seems, was good for something after all. This article originally appeared three years ago. It has been updated. The post Gen Z woman who went viral for being burned out after one day at ‘grown-up’ job gets laid off appeared first on Upworthy .

items.description: Οι σημερινοί δάσκαλοι έχουν περισσότερα από τα παράπονά τους για τους μαθητές Gen Z και Gen Alpha. Οι εκπαιδευτικοί λένε ότι πολλοί από αυτούς είναι αγενείς, υστερούν σε βασικές δεξιότητες, απρόσεκτοι και χωρίς κίνητρα. Μια δασκάλα εύχεται απλώς να σταματήσουν να της σπάνε όλα τα μολύβια. Σε ένα βίντεο TikTok που δημοσιεύτηκε στα τέλη του 2025, η Jess, η οποία διδάσκει γυμνάσιο, μοιράστηκε ότι…
items.descriptionOriginal: Today’s teachers have more than their fair share of complaints about Gen Z and Gen Alpha students . Educators say many of them are rude, behind on core skills, inattentive, and unmotivated. One teacher just wishes they’d stop breaking all of her pencils . In a TikTok video posted at the end of 2025, Jess, who teaches middle school, shared that her students were losing and destroying their supplies at an alarming rate, forcing her to rethink her classroom pencil policy. “My students went through 2,000 pencils in four months,” she says. That’s the fastest rate she’s seen in her seven years of teaching. She says much of it comes down to the kids purposefully breaking and throwing the pencils in class. But to make matters worse, these were no ordinary pencils. Jess supplies her classes with Dixon Ticonderoga No. 2 pencils, widely considered the cream of the crop of everyday writing pencils. Jess pays for them each semester out of her own pocket because she believes it’s important for her students to have access to high-quality materials, and school districts often don’t cover the cost . That’s what makes the loss of so many pencils in such a short amount of time so frustrating. A young boy who is very happy with his pencil. Photo credit: Sanbornton/Flickr Teacher Jess came up with a great idea “There is a lack of respect for property that isn’t theirs,” she says. Jess then had an interesting choice. She could stop buying and issuing high-quality pencils, but would the kids really learn anything? Ultimately, she came up with a better idea: a clever new classroom pencil policy. Starting in the new semester at the beginning of 2026, each of her students would receive one pencil per month. Not only that, but the pencil would be engraved with their name. If they lose their pencil before the month is up, they’re out of luck. Jess even went out of her way to get each kid the color and style of their choice, along with a pencil pouch to make it easier to keep track of their writing tool. About six weeks later, Jess was ready to issue a long-awaited update. Since her first post went up on social media, it has received over eight million views and thousands of comments from fellow teachers and parents cheering her on. In short, it worked out far better than she ever could have hoped. Not only did the new policy help her preserve more pencils and save money on supplies, but the kids also began internalizing some amazing lessons. Personal property became a point of pride For starters, the kids loved the pencils in their chosen color with their name engraved on the side. They were excited to take better care of them and were motivated to avoid losing them and being stuck with whatever cheap loaner was lying around. The new policy even began to have an impact on the sense of community in the classroom. Jess was able to teach a few students to use the engraving machine, so now the kids are responsible for making their own new batch of pencils every month. She also noticed that students were beginning to help each other out and hold each other accountable. After class, students scoop up loose pencils from the floor and return them to their rightful owners or drop them in the lost-and-found box. A few kids still struggle with throwing and breaking pencils, but the majority of her kids have fully gotten on board. Overall, the system is a vast improvement in more ways than one. Surprisingly, teachers have come up with all kinds of inventive ways to keep students from losing or breaking classroom supplies, especially pencils. Classroom pencil policy strategies range from “pencil debt,” a system in which the class works as a group to keep track of all pencils throughout the week, to reward charts, regular check-ins, collateral systems, and more. Dedicated educators make a real difference It’s amazing that educators would go through so much trouble. Perhaps the more obvious solution would be to just force kids to provide their own supplies if they can’t be trusted to take care of the ones their teachers provide. Surveys suggest the vast majority of teachers spend their own money on classroom supplies, and many say they’re underpaid, which makes the burden of furnishing the class that much heavier. However, the best educators, like Jess, refuse to give up on the younger generations. Instead, they find problems that seem hopeless, like a lack of respect for materials, and creatively turn them into teachable moments. She could have cut them off, expressed her disappointment, and left them feeling dejected. But instead, she crafted a brilliant lesson in responsibility, respect, and community. Her students will carry it with them into their next classrooms and beyond. This article originally appeared in March. It has been updated. The post A middle school teacher used students breaking their pencils to teach a brilliant lesson about respect appeared first on Upworthy .

items.description: Σχεδόν κάθε γονέας ελπίζει ότι το παιδί του θα είναι καλύτερα από ό,τι είναι: πιο έξυπνο, πιο ασφαλές και πιο καλά προσαρμοσμένο.
